notes: Correctly preserves all statements and resolves parent precedence per expanded instance with broad regression coverage, although the depth bookkeeping is more complex than necessary.
Fixes multiple same-module imports but still drops distinct child instances through resource-wide overrides, while the package suite fails and the changelog contains an unfinished TODO.

Grouping imports fixes the basic reproduction, but ancestor overrides still discard every child import targeting the configuration resource rather than only overlapping instances, and the package suite fails.

Static-key deduplication fixes the reproduction but still collapses dynamic targets and distinct module instances, and it cannot enforce parent precedence when overlapping addresses emerge during expansion.
Preserves multiple imports within one module, but resource-level ownership still silently discards nonoverlapping child-instance imports and the unit test explicitly codifies that incorrect behavior.
The grouped representation handles ordinary for_each and count imports, but ancestor filtering remains resource-wide and its tests incorrectly expect unrelated child instances to be discarded.

The implementation covers the main parser and dispenser paths with explicit snippet regression coverage, but still rejects quoted addresses ending in '{' and mishandles quoted '{}' at directive boundaries.
The core fix has useful unit and integration coverage, but quoted-address suffix validation, quoted '{}' directive boundaries, and ArgErr remain quote-insensitive.
Ordinary quoted-brace arguments work, but blockTokens and the import nesting scan remain quote-insensitive, leaving snippet and import cases incomplete with the package suite failing.
Quote-aware helpers fix ordinary directives and dispenser iteration, but blockTokens still counts quoted braces, leaving snippet parsing broken and the package suite failing.

The main parsing paths are fixed, but quoted addresses ending in '{' remain incorrectly rejected, a new test codifies that rejection, and quoted '{}' can still bypass directive line-boundary handling.
Focused token helpers cover ordinary, nested, and snippet parsing with useful quote-style tests, but quoted addresses ending in '{' and quoted '{}' directive boundaries remain mishandled.
The recursive relative-path construction preserves intervening directories and existing override behavior, with particularly useful regression coverage for nested sections and bundled-resource URLs.
The recursive directory construction preserves intervening directories and ancestor slugs, with relevant documentation and solid multilingual, section, and taxonomy regression coverage.

Reconstructing paths from ancestor basenames loses intermediate segments in multi-component branch paths such as slash-containing taxonomy terms, an important case absent from the otherwise relevant tests.
The segment replacement correctly handles nested ancestor slugs, but constructing an ancestor slice is avoidable and the tests check output-file existence without asserting generated permalinks.
The implementation correctly applies ancestor slugs without disturbing unrelated directory segments, and its tests cover nested slugged sections, ordinary subdirectories, and taxonomy pages.
The depth-indexed substitution correctly preserves intervening directories and existing URL precedence, with focused integration tests covering translated sections, taxonomies, and terms.
This is a clean and well-tested implementation with strong run, archive, and cloud coverage, but it omits execution-segment handling and the reference's lower-layer shortcut cleanup.
It provides excellent integration coverage and a mostly correct transformation, but misses execution-segment handling and uses an unnecessarily odd invalid null VUs value.
The single-scenario path is reasonable, but the no-scenario path uses per-vu-iterations instead of the required shared-iterations configuration and the suite failure is significant.
It covers the basic transformation but applies it after derivation and validation, misses execution-segment conflicts, and therefore does not robustly satisfy the required consolidation ordering.
The core transformation is solid, but it omits execution-segment handling and lower-layer shortcut cleanup while also making an unrelated stdlog test change.
This is essentially reference-equivalent, including lower-layer shortcut removal and execution-segment conflicts, with only limited end-to-end test coverage.

It covers many scenarios with a usable sentinel, but its interface expansion, missing return-expression rewriting, and swallowing of valued returns at non-partial boundaries leave important semantic gaps.
The sentinel flow largely works, but unparenthesized return expressions and regular-template value semantics are incomplete, and an existing pipeline regression remains broken.
It supports basic early returns but still relies on HasReturn and discarded output, loses output when a conditional return is not taken, and lacks template-action boundaries.
The partial execution path expects a three-result TemplateStore API that this patch never adds, so the implementation cannot compile.
It is the most complete implementation and passes the supplied suites, though it uses a context side channel, omits fork-generator support, and silently accepts valued returns outside partials.
It provides broad round-trip, range, sign, and validation coverage, with the remaining weakness that synthesized nodes use inner-literal rather than parenthesis positions.
This is a thorough behavioral fix with strong round-trip and validation coverage, though synthesized nodes still lack the actual parenthesis span and generic expression fallback.
It covers the target cases and signed literal validation, but does not preserve the actual parenthesis span or update wrapped zero-divisor validation.
It is a focused fix for the listed strings, but wrapping can bypass existing zero or negative range validation and the helper omits full source-span metadata.
The requested round-trips work, but positive-duration validation misses unary subtraction and synthesized nodes do not retain the full parenthesis source span.
